ideas: Basic facts needed before deeper thinking
Information is easy to look up now
model: I think memorisation still has its place, but it shouldn't be the main way students learn. Some basic knowledge really does need to be learned by heart. You can't do maths quickly without knowing your times tables, and you can't speak a language fluently without memorising vocabulary. It gives you a solid foundation for critical thinking. However, in the past, schools in Vietnam used to rely far too much on memorisation. When I was at school, we would learn essays parrot-fashion and repeat them in exams, without really understanding the ideas. Today, students have almost any fact at their fingertips, because they can look it up on their phones in seconds. So schools no longer need to fill children's heads with dates and definitions. Of course, some people argue that if you don't remember anything, you can't think deeply about it, and I partly agree. In my view, memorisation and understanding should go hand in hand, rather than one replacing the other.
